subject: rsf.fit() functionality for time-varying raster stacks

messages.author: 037c64fcb3960038
messages.subject: rsf.fit() functionality for time-varying raster stacks
parts:
Hi there,

I'm hoping to use the weighted RSF approach for my habitat selection analysis on false killer whales. However, nearly all of my covariates (rasters) are going to be time-specific, since oceanographic features are so dynamic. 

For example, I have daily rasters for sea surface temperature, and thus the sea surface temperature raster to use in the RSF will depend on the date of a particular set of locations in a given track.

I see in the current documentation for rsf.fit() that, for R, either a named list of rasters or time-varying raster stacks can be supplied, but that the latter has not been tested. Has there been any progress on this? I did try supplying a raster stack object of my daily SST rasters to the rsf.fit() function, but got an error ("R is not a named list of rasters"). I made a named list of the raster stack (rlist <- list(stack); names(rlist) <- "sst"), but got a different error from rsf.fit(): "Error in if (raster::is.factor(R[[i]])) { : the condition has length > 1"

I'm assuming that perhaps this hasn't been developed enough yet, but if it has that would be great to know. Otherwise, I'll likely have to fit my RSFs outside of ctmm, as I can't really avoid temporally-varying covariates.

Thank you in advance!
Michaela
